title: Bumrah Out of Sri Lanka Tests; J&K's Auqib Nabi Gets Maiden India Call-Up
excerpt: The Jammu & Kashmir fast bowler, who took 104 wickets in two Ranji Trophy seasons and helped his state win its maiden title, becomes the first cricketer from the region selected for India's senior Test squad.
body:
• Jasprit Bumrah has been ruled out of India's two-Test series in Sri Lanka due to a persistent left knee injury sustained during the ODI series against England.
  • Jammu & Kashmir pacer Auqib Nabi replaces Bumrah, becoming the first cricketer from the region to earn a senior India Test call-up.
  • Nabi took 104 wickets across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons, including 60 in 2025-26 as J&K won their first-ever title.
  • The series begins August 15 in Galle under captain Shubman Gill, with the second Test in Colombo starting August 23.

India pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah has been ruled out of the upcoming two-Test series against Sri Lanka, the BCCI confirmed on Monday. In his place, uncapped Jammu & Kashmir fast bowler Auqib Nabi has earned a maiden call-up to the senior squad — making him the first cricketer from the region to be selected for India's Test team.

Bumrah sustained a left knee injury while fielding during the one-day international series against England in Cardiff in July. He was initially included in the squad subject to a final fitness assessment and had been undergoing rehabilitation at the BCCI's Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru. However, persistent discomfort forced the selectors to withdraw him and name Nabi as a direct replacement.

From Ranji Trophy Hero to National Squad

Nabi's selection caps a remarkable rise through Indian domestic cricket. The 26-year-old has claimed 104 wickets across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons, including a standout haul of 60 wickets in 2025-26 — the most by any bowler in the tournament — as he spearheaded Jammu & Kashmir to their maiden Ranji Trophy title.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=M-nyi_ldmzQ

His domestic form earned him a spot on the India A tour of Sri Lanka in June and July, where he picked up six wickets in two first-class matches in Galle. That experience on Sri Lankan pitches gives him a practical edge heading into the Test series.

"Auqib's call-up is significant, considering he got 60 wickets to become the highest wicket-taker while guiding Jammu and Kashmir to their maiden Ranji Trophy triumph."

— IANS report on Nabi's India A selection

Squad Reshuffle Beyond Bumrah

Bumrah is not the only absentee. All-rounder Washington Sundar has also been ruled out of at least the first Test, with 33-year-old Madhya Pradesh off-spinner Saransh Jain named as his replacement. Jain, who has played domestic cricket since 2014, impressed on the India A tour to Sri Lanka, scoring 70 runs and taking six wickets in two innings during a first-class match in Galle.

Batter Sai Sudharsan's participation remains subject to clearance from the BCCI's medical team. If fit, he adds depth to a batting lineup that already includes Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul, and Rishabh Pant.

The full 15-member squad reads: Shubman Gill (captain), KL Rahul (vice-captain), Yashasvi Jaiswal, Rishabh Pant (wk), Sai Sudharsan, Dhruv Jurel (wk), Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav, Manav Suthar, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, Devdutt Padikkal, Saransh Jain, and Auqib Nabi.

What It Means for J&K Cricket

For Jammu & Kashmir, Nabi's selection is a landmark moment. The region has produced talented cricketers over the decades — Parvez Rasool became the first from J&K to play for India in a limited-overs match in 2014 — but a Test call-up has remained elusive until now. Nabi's rapid ascent, from leading J&K's Ranji Trophy charge to rubbing shoulders with India's senior squad, underscores the BCCI's renewed emphasis on rewarding domestic performance.

For the diaspora, Nabi's story carries resonance beyond cricket. It speaks to the expanding pipeline of talent emerging from regions historically underrepresented in Indian sport, and the growing infrastructure that makes such breakthroughs possible.

Looking Ahead

India begin the series at Galle International Stadium on August 15, a venue that has traditionally favored spin. The second Test follows at the Sinhalese Sports Club Ground in Colombo starting August 23. Both matches count toward the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 cycle.

Without Bumrah's pace and control, India's seam attack will lean heavily on Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna, with Nabi and Gurnoor Brar providing backup. Whether Nabi gets a debut cap will depend on conditions and team balance, but his presence in the squad is already a statement — both for him and for J&K cricket.
